The hardware

The earpiece Aritzia already owns.

Atelier, by Joule is software, not hardware. It loads onto the earpieces boutiques already use — so there is nothing to buy, nothing new to carry, and nothing an associate has to be taught to hold.

Three controls do the whole job on a shift. Scroll to see each one.

Anatomy

Seven parts. Three of them matter on the floor.

Every part of this unit already exists in the boutique today. Atelier adds a voice layer on top of it, and the interface an associate actually touches comes down to a dial, a mute button and an indicator light.

None of the three needs to be looked at. All of them can be found by touch, with both hands full.

Control 01 · Clock-in

On, off, and a light that says you’re reachable.

Earpieces are picked up at clock-in and powered on once. The indicator light is the only confirmation an associate needs: lit means on shift and reachable.

Off shift, the unit is off and nothing can reach it. That is deliberate — it keeps work messages off personal phones and out of unpaid hours, which matters most in the US, where about 62% of Aritzia’s revenue sits.

Press → powerSteady blue → on shiftDark → off shift

Control 02 · Set level

One dial, because a boutique is never one volume.

The dial sets how loudly a teammate’s voice arrives. A fitting room at open is not the same room at peak on a Saturday, and the level that works for one is unusable in the other.

It stays a physical, knurled dial for one reason: it can be found and turned by feel — mid-conversation, with bundles in hand, without breaking eye contact with a client.

Detented rotaryTen stepsSet by touch

Control 03 · Mute

Press once, and the client’s conversation stays in the room.

Atelier listens for a teammate’s name or role at the start of speech and drops everything else on the device. Mute is the physical guarantee on top of that: press it and the microphone is off, the light turns amber, and an associate can confirm at a glance that nothing is leaving the earpiece.

Press it again to come back on.

Audio is never stored. Only the routed request is transcribed — the recording is discarded.

In use

Say a name, and only that person hears you.

AO → BA“Dora, can you grab the Effortless Pant in a 4, black, for suite three?”
BA → AO“On it.”

An Atelier Operator in the change rooms says the request out loud. The Boutique Associate running the floor hears it in their own ear, in their teammate’s own voice — no screen, no refresh, no app to open.

And no broadcast channel. Fifteen associates shouting over each other is the failure that moved Aritzia onto an app in the first place; targeted routing is how we avoid repeating it.

And then

Every hand-off becomes data Aritzia can act on.

The earpiece is where the request is spoken. SAP Business Data Cloud is where it lands. Each routed request is transcribed into a record — item, size, colour, boutique, found or not found — which turns the fitting room into a demand signal that sales and inventory data alone cannot see.

Existing earpiece→Joule voice routing→SAP Business Data Cloud
